message.content: On rounds I saw staff leave medication carts unlocked in a hallway. Has OIG cited this kind of thing? Point me to the reports.

The OIG has reported several findings that medication carts were left unlocked or unattended in hallways and other areas.  Below are the reports that cite this problem and include the OIG’s recommendations to secure the carts.

| Report Number | Title (link) | Date published | Finding quoted |
|---------------|--------------|----------------|----------------|
| **15‑00606‑495** | [Combined Assessment Program Review of the Battle Creek VA Medical Center, Battle Creek, Michigan](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-battle-2) | 31 Aug 2015 | “We recommended that employees secure medication carts when not in use and that facility managers monitor compliance.” |
| **13‑03653‑91** | [Combined Assessment Program Review of the Atlanta VA Medical Center, Decatur, Georgia](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-atlanta-va-1) | 12 Mar 2014 | “We recommended that processes be strengthened to ensure that medication carts are secured at all times and that compliance be monitored.” |
| **13‑00279‑156** | [Combined Assessment Program Review of the VA Palo Alto Health Care System, Palo Alto, California](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-va-palo-2) | 28 Mar 2013 | Same recommendation to keep carts locked and monitor compliance. |
| **15‑00607‑483** | [Combined Assessment Program Review of the San Francisco VA Health Care System, San Francisco, California](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-san-4) | 24 Aug 2015 | “We recommended that employees secure medication carts when not in use and that facility managers monitor compliance.” |
| **15‑00071‑158** | [Combined Assessment Program Review of the West Palm Beach VA Medical Center, West Palm Beach, Florida](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-west-palm-2) | 31 Mar 2015 | The report notes two medication carts were **unlocked** and unattended on a CLC‑N unit and cites recommendation 8 to secure carts. |
| **20‑03593‑140** | [Care and Oversight Deficiencies Related to Multiple Homicides at the Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center, Clarksburg, West Virginia](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/hotline-healthcare-inspection/care-and-oversight-deficiencies-related-multiple-homicides) | 11 May 2021 | “In 2018, medication carts on ward 3A were not consistently secured as some were unlocked and unattended…” |
| **12‑03075‑52** | [Combined Assessment Program Review of the Miami VA Healthcare System, Miami, Florida](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-miami-va-1) | 7 Dec 2012 | “Staff was instructed that medications are to be secured at all times and not left on top of medication carts or in unlocked rooms.” |

**What the OIG says**  
In each of these reports the OIG observed medication carts left unlocked, often in hallways or other unsecured locations, and issued recommendations that the facility:

* Secure the carts (lock them) whenever they are not in use.  
* Monitor compliance through random checks, rounding, or audits.  
* Repair or replace carts with non‑functioning locks.  

These findings span multiple VA facilities and years, showing that unlocked medication carts have been a recurring safety issue identified by the OIG.  The data are current as of **4 Nov 2026**.
